neighbours.label: result / purpose connectives in practical advice or narrative ('so that', 'That way,', 'So') and set time phrases ('when it came time'), points where a 'when …' clause can follow; the output direction promotes ' when'
fire: I write the date on every jar. That way, when I open the cupboard, I can see which one is oldest.
Farmers flood the fields in spring so that the soil will stay moist when the seeds are sown.
She practised the piece every night. So when the concert came, her hands knew every note.
Pack your bag the evening before so that you don't have to rush at the last minute.
Keep a spare key with a neighbour. That way, if you lock yourself out, you can still get in.
They trained together all winter, but when it came time to name the captain, the coach picked a newcomer.
Set two alarms so that you wake up even if the first one fails.
He saved a little each month. That way, when the roof needed repair, the money was there.
quiet: I write the date on every jar and keep the jars in the cupboard above the sink.
Farmers flood the fields in spring and the soil stays moist for weeks.
She practised the piece every night and her hands knew every note.
Pack your bag the evening before and leave it by the front door.
Keep a spare key with a neighbour who lives on the same street.
They trained together all winter and the coach picked a newcomer as captain.
Set two alarms and put the phone on the far side of the room.
He saved a little each month and paid for the roof repair himself.

notes: Probes: so that / That way / So / when it came time 0.39-0.74; a plain statement 0.005.
